entries.gap: Prompt injection can rewrite workflow authority.
entries.mitigation: Mandatory kernel, untrusted-content policy, immutable attachment map during task execution.
entries.evidence: Structural composition test and injection-in-issue scenario.

entries.gap: A persistent graph can bleed across branch, worktree, or dirty source state.
entries.mitigation: Task/branch provenance and selective freshness validation.
entries.evidence: Helper freshness tests and branch-switch/dirty-worktree scenarios.

entries.gap: Investigation can create pseudo-hypotheses or endless retries.
entries.mitigation: Prediction ledger and information/budget circuit breaker with ownership transfer.

entries.gap: Delegation can exceed the task's uncertainty or omit a material specialist risk.
entries.mitigation: Minimal routing with explicit risk/capability justification.

entries.gap: Local changes can produce architecture drift or premature abstractions.
entries.mitigation: Ponytail review trigger and architecture-pressure detection.

entries.gap: Author context can bias review; test failures can be misclassified.
entries.mitigation: Fresh evidence package and test reliability gate.

entries.gap: Durable knowledge can leak secrets, raw data, or repository-local state into Git.
entries.mitigation: Single writer workflow, strict schema, redaction, local exclude, and Git guard.

entries.gap: Graph expansion can overstate evidence or turn into an infrastructure project.
entries.mitigation: Evidence/confidence scopes, Level-1 progressive retrieval, external pointers, and file-only overlay by default.

entries.gap: Database access can become a mutation or context-explosion path.
entries.mitigation: Read-only evidence layer with explicit projected columns, bounded rows, structured excerpts, and lightweight provenance.
entries.evidence: Knowledge grounding policy and DB scenarios.

entries.gap: A local fix can hide material adjacent regression risk or cumulative responsibility drift.
entries.mitigation: Bounded adjacent-risk verification and compressed architecture-pressure signals.
entries.evidence: Verification workflow, graph index metadata, and regression scenarios.

entries.gap: Attachment failures or skipped graph grounding can allow domain mutation on incomplete context.
entries.mitigation: Required attachment gate, explicit graph presence/absence, and approval-plus-grounding execution gate.
entries.evidence: Grounding workflow rules, graph-state helper test, and behavioral scenarios.

entries.gap: Generic minimal delegation can override stronger specialist requirements and blur implementation ownership.
entries.mitigation: Explicit instruction precedence, primary-executor ownership, and compact phase transitions.
entries.evidence: Orchestrator ownership rules and behavioral scenarios.

entries.gap: A reviewer with implementation history can be presented as independent and permit high-risk publication without independent judgment.
entries.mitigation: Fresh-context review requirement, Confirmation Review classification, and high-risk publication gate.
entries.evidence: Code reviewer procedure and behavioral scenarios.

entries.gap: Copied skill discovery, dirty provenance, legacy restamping, or broken links can make repository knowledge look more trustworthy than it is.
entries.mitigation: Canonical bundle resolution, committed-path provenance enforcement, explicit trust states, linked-record validation, and coverage-gap reporting.
entries.evidence: Bundle/context helper tests and knowledge-grounding scenarios.
